title: Kubernetes admission controls and runtime feature gating for private deployments
author: Asha Mehta
content:
Overview:

Purpose: This document standardizes Kubernetes admission controls (mutating and validating), policy enforcement, and runtime feature-gating patterns we use for Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It defines a minimal policy catalog, rollout and test procedures, monitoring checkpoints, and operator runbook actions for feature flag driven runtime changes (e.g., KV cache migration, batching, quantization fallback, and model swap safemode).

Scope:
- Applies to all private deployment clusters managed by Redwood (tenant-facing control plane, operator-managed runtime clusters, and edge appliances).
- Focuses on admission-time governance and runtime feature flags that affect inference behavior and tenant isolation.
- Does NOT replace host-level security guidance (see /security-and-compliance) or the private deploy operator installation guide.

Motivation:
Private deployments require a stricter guardrail set than hosted environments: we must ensure consistent runtime safety across heterogeneous Kubernetes distributions, enforce tenant boundaries at admission time, and allow controlled dynamic toggles of runtime behavior without full cluster upgrades. Admission controls + feature flags let us:
- Prevent risky pod specs reaching the runtime (e.g., privileged containers, hostPath exposures).
- Enforce resource and QoS contracts before scheduling (avoid noisy neighbor regressions).
- Gate rollout of runtime changes to a small canary set of nodes/tenants, with automated rollback on regressions.

Architecture and components:
- MutatingAdmissionWebhook: injects required sidecars and runtime annotations (e.g., instance-labels, sidecar proxies, seccomp profile selectors).
- ValidatingAdmissionWebhook: blocks disallowed fields (e.g., hostNetwork, hostPath unless allowlist) and enforces tenant-specific pod resource guarantees.
- OPA (Gatekeeper) policies: declarative constraint templates that express security, network, and resource policies.
- Runtime feature flag service: lightweight HTTP endpoint (internal) used by the operator to toggle features per-tenant or per-node-label. Features are also encoded as ConfigMaps with a simple schema and a revisioned change history.
- Canary orchestration runner: small controller that stages feature flags to a canary cohort, runs smoke tests, and promotes/rolls back automatically.

Minimal policy catalog (recommended defaults):
- DisallowPrivilegedContainers: deny pod.spec.containers[*].securityContext.privileged == true
- RequiredSeccompProfile: enforce seccomp annotation 'runtime.seccomp.restrictive' unless tenant is on allowlist.
- NoHostPathUnlessSigned: deny hostPath mounts unless the image is signed and the hostPath appears in the customer-approved inventory.
- PodResourceFloor: require requests.cpu >= 100m and requests.memory >= 256Mi for inference service pods.
- ImmutableModelMount: prevent mutable hostPath or emptyDir mounts for /models and /kv unless operator flag model-refresh-unsafe=true.
- EgressWhitelist: validate that pod-level egress addresses conform to tenant egress contract (VPC-peered endpoints, telemetry gateway).

Policy table (human-readable):
Name | Enforced by | Failure action | Owner | Escalation
DisallowPrivilegedContainers | ValidatingWebhook | reject | runtime-security | eng-sre
RequiredSeccompProfile | Gatekeeper | reject | runtime-security | eng-sre
NoHostPathUnlessSigned | Gatekeeper + webhook | reject + evidence log | ops-field | eng-field-ops
PodResourceFloor | Webhook | reject | runtime-platform | eng-platform
ImmutableModelMount | Webhook | reject | runtime-platform | eng-platform
EgressWhitelist | Gatekeeper | audit -> reject after 30d | security | security-team

Implementation notes and examples:
- Mutating webhook connector (snippet): injects the sidecar service mesh proxy and operator annotations used by the canary runner. Example YAML (abbreviated):

apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: MutatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  name: redwood-mutating-webhook
webhooks:
  - name: inject-runtime-sidecars.redwood.internal
    clientConfig:
      service:
        name: runtime-webhook
        namespace: redwood-system
        path: /mutate
    rules:
      - operations: ["CREATE"]
        apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        resources: ["pods"]
    admissionReviewVersions: ["v1"]
    sideEffects: None

- Gatekeeper constraint example (rego-like policy summarized):

package redwood.allowed

violation["hostPathNotAllowed"] {
  input.review.object.spec.volumes[_].hostPath
  not input.review.object.metadata.annotations["redwood/hostpath-approved"]
}

- Feature flag ConfigMap schema (single-line example):

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: runtime-feature-flags
  namespace: redwood-system
data:
  feature-flags.json: |-
    {"kv_cache_migration": {"state": "gradual", "cohort_selector": "nodeLabel=kv-candidate", "started_at": "2026-09-01T00:00:00Z", "revision": "v3"}, "quantization_fallback": {"state": "on", "safety_threshold_rpm": "0.98"} }

Operational workflows:
1) Feature rollout (canary -> staged -> global):
  1. Author change and create new ConfigMap with incremented revision. Add human-friendly changelog in annotation.
  2. Stage to canary cohort via cohort_selector (nodeLabel or tenant label).
  3. Trigger synthetic smoke tests: 50 small generation requests, 10 embedding queries, latency and correctness checks against baseline prompt set.
  4. Observe for 60 minutes; required pass criteria: 95th percentile latency not worse than baseline + 15%, error rate < 0.25%, quality regression measured via eval harness score delta <= -0.02.
  5. If smoke tests pass, extend cohort to 20% of nodes/tenants for 6 hours; repeat checks.
  6. If staged pass, promote to 100% with a scheduled quiet window and longer monitoring (24 hours).
  7. If any stage fails, automated rollback to previous revision and create incident with priority P1 if customer-facing SLA impacted.

2) Quick rollback criteria (operator-triggered):
  - 95th percentile latency regression > 30% or absolute increase > 250ms for inference endpoints; OR
  - request error rate > 1% sustained for 5 minutes; OR
  - model output quality alerts from eval monitors (regression > 0.05).

3) Admission policy change procedure (for Gatekeeper/OPA templates):
  - Create PR in infra-policy repo with policy change + unit tests (rego test).
  - Deploy to staging cluster Gatekeeper in audit-only mode for 72 hours and gather violations.
  - Host a 30-minute policy review with security and platform owners if violations exceed 5 unique tenants.
  - After signoff, schedule a controlled enforcement window and publish change notes to customer-facing T&Cs if required.

Observability and SLOs for feature rollouts and admission controls:
- Admission enforcement latency (webhook avg latency): target < 25ms p50, < 100ms p99. Alert if p99 > 200ms for > 5m.
- Policy violation spike: alert when new violation rate > 10x baseline or > 5 incidents in 1h.
- Feature rollout guardrails:
  - Latency regression: alert if p95 increases by > 15% vs baseline over rollout window.
  - Error spike: alert if 5xx rate > 0.5% on inference endpoints during rollout.
  - Quality monitors: push evaluation results to the quality-guardrails service; alert if eval delta exceeds configured threshold.

Testing matrix (minimum):
- Unit: rego policies (local tests), webhook unit tests.
- Integration: deploy webhook and Gatekeeper in a cluster with sample tenant manifests. Run canary runner in dry-run mode.
- E2E: load test with synthetic traffic that approximates 80th percentile tenant load plus occasional spikes. Verify rollback behaves as expected.

CLI & debugging tips:
- Viewing admission traces: kubectl get events -n redwood-system --field-selector reason=FailedAdmission.
- Live webhook latency: kubectl logs deploy/runtime-webhook -n redwood-system | grep "admission-latency"
- Gatekeeper violations: kubectl get constraints --all-namespaces; use gatekeeper-audit to export historical violations.
- Force rollback of feature flag: kubectl apply -f runtime-feature-flags-v2.yaml && annotate rollback-reason="observability-regression"; the canary controller will detect the revision change and reconcile quickly.

Incident runbook (high level):
- Trigger: monitoring alerts (latency, error rate, quality).
- Triage (T+0-5min): oncall checks canary cohort and verifies ConfigMap revision; determine whether change aligns to active rollout.
- Mitigation (T+5-15min): if associated with a revision deployed < 60m ago, rollback to previous revision via the controller 'rollback' endpoint (/api/v1/flags/rollback) or apply previous ConfigMap.
- Communication (T+15-30min): notify customer success and any affected customers using templated messages; update status page if customer-facing SLA affected.
- Post-incident (within 72h): produce a short incident summary covering the root cause, detection timeline, mitigation steps, and follow-up actions (e.g., stricter test case, additional synthetic checks).

Ownership and responsibilities:
- runtime-platform: owns the mutating/validating webhook code, canary runner, and ConfigMap schema.
- runtime-security: owns Gatekeeper constraints, security review, and policy signoff.
- eng-sre: owns monitoring dashboards, alert rules, and oncall runbooks.
- eng-field-ops: handles tenant allowlists and customer special-case approvals.

Backwards compatibility and audit evidence:
- All policy changes must be logged to the policy-change ledger (immutable S3 bucket) with diff, author, and timestamp.
- Feature flag ConfigMaps are revisioned and kept for 90 days; we snapshot and store canary test results alongside each revision.

Appendix: common regression thresholds (for quick reference)
- Latency: p95 increase > 15% or absolute > 500ms (whichever is smaller) triggers staged rollback.
- Error rate: > 1% sustained for 5m triggers rollback.
- Quality eval delta: drop in eval score > 0.05 requires immediate rollback and forensic snapshot.

References and links:
- Gatekeeper docs and our policy templates: /eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures/policy-templates
- Canary runner controller API: /eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/canary-controller-api-2026
- Quality guardrails and eval harness: /applied-ml-and-evals/quality-guardrails

Notes and caveats:
- Admission webhooks must be highly available across API server endpoints. Use node anti-affinity for runtime-webhook pods and scaled replicas (minimum 3 in multi-zone clusters).
- For air-gapped deployments: host Path allowlists must be prepopulated via the field onboarding manifest.

Contact: runtime-platform@redwood.example.com for implementation questions; runtime-security@redwood.example.com for policy review.
